key.name: window-rules-v2
key.summary: Where the automatic decoration is reversed, per window kind
key.description: A correction the user made for one window kind. Each rule describes a kind through the window's stable structural attributes: the application identity, the client type, the window type, whether the window has a parent, whether it is attached to that parent, whether it can be resized, whether it declares its own shadow margin ring, and whether the compositor frames it itself. A fixed-size window also records its logical width and height, because those cannot change; a resizable window records no size, because its size is not stable. The state names the axes whose automatic decision the user reversed, in canonical order, e.g. 'corners,shadow'; an axis not named follows the automatic decision, and a state naming nothing is the same as no rule. Structural facts (a non-decorable window type, maximized or fullscreen state, unresizable windows, SSD frames) are capability, not choice, and a reversed axis never overrides them. The rule also carries the title of the window it was picked from, which the preferences window shows and matching never reads. The resize axis is about the grab band, and reversing it is bidirectional: it widens the band to the native 12 pixels out on every side, and 24 along the edge at each corner, or retracts the band the reading drew; a GTK4 window declaring at least 12 pixels on every side already owns a native-width handle, so the heuristic leaves it alone.

key.name: prefer-crisp-text
key.description: Skip rounded corners on fractional scale monitors (retaining shadow) to avoid text blur and resampling overhead.
